Small place. Serious ice cream.

SCROLL

A one-room ice cream shop on Istedgade, making a single new flavour every week — nothing else on the menu.

No branches, no freezer case of thirty tubs. One counter, one chef, one flavour worth the walk.

Istedgade 107, 1650 København V

The little ice cream shop

Eleven square metres. Usually a queue.

  • Room for four people inside at a time — everyone else waits on the pavement.
  • One flavour a week, gone when it's gone.
  • Open every day from noon — Sundays to Thursdays till ten, Fridays and Saturdays till eleven.
The whole shop
11m²

Counter, machine, and one very small freezer — that's the entire floor plan.

This week

Five ways it's gone lately

Craft

Every batch is small enough to taste before it leaves the machine.

01
Dairy

Local, unhomogenised

Milk and cream from a single dairy on Zealand, collected twice a week — never frozen before it reaches the base.

02
Sourcing

Foraged and seasonal

Sea buckthorn from the coast, rye from the bakery next door, whatever the chef found worth building a week around.

03
Batching

Eighteen litres at a time

Small enough to churn, taste, and adjust by hand — no flavour goes out until it's right.

04
Menu

One flavour, fully committed

No fallback tub of vanilla. If it's not good enough to be the only scoop in the shop, it doesn't go in the case.

The queue

The queue outside isn't a problem to fix. It's most of the fun.

People compare notes on what's scooping this week before they've even reached the counter. Bring a friend — you'll have twenty minutes to catch up.
